decisions.title: Backend language
decisions.chosen: Use Rust for the hosted backend and workers.
decisions.rationale: Earlier preference for compile-time ownership checks and memory control.
tradeoffs: Additional Rust learning and async complexity.

decisions.title: Backend language
decisions.chosen: Use Go for the hosted backend and controlled database tools.
decisions.rationale: Remote database operations and model inference dominate expected waiting; simpler development fits the near-term deadline. No comparative benchmark exists.
decisions.strongestAlternative: Keep Rust with the same TypeScript investigator.
tradeoffs: Accept garbage collection and explicit shared-state discipline.
Gain simpler expected development; no measured capacity guarantee.

decisions.title: Investigator workflow
decisions.chosen: Keep one TypeScript/LangGraph investigator with PostgreSQL-backed operational state and checkpoints.
decisions.rationale: Retain structured loops, branches and visual debugging while Go enforces tool authority.
decisions.strongestAlternative: Implement the investigator directly in the backend language.
tradeoffs: A second runtime and internal API boundary.
LangGraph does not supply diagnosis logic or exactly-once database effects.

decisions.title: Fully hosted operation
decisions.chosen: Pooltune operates its services; customers connect existing Supabase projects.
decisions.rationale: Operation must continue without an open laptop or browser; customers should not rent another server.
tradeoffs: Pooltune must operate workers, credentials and selected diagnostic storage.
Customer records stay in their DB, but diagnostic evidence may leave it.

decisions.title: Reuse existing evidence
decisions.chosen: Reuse sufficient current evidence; add experiments only for decision-relevant gaps.
decisions.rationale: Avoid redundant load on customer databases while preserving outcome verification.
decisions.strongestAlternative: Repeat a fixed benchmark suite for every investigation.
tradeoffs: Freshness and comparable context must be checked.
Insufficient evidence can require waiting or an inconclusive result.

decisions.title: Live-trial policy remains open
decisions.chosen: Propose owner-enabled live trials after evidence screening, with one candidate at a time and explicit resource conditions.
decisions.rationale: Actual index performance needs a physical index and comparable measurements. Jared expressed support; exact limits and recovery are not approved.
decisions.strongestAlternative: Require a representative isolated test environment before production changes.
tradeoffs: Live trials consume customer DB resources before benefit is proven.
A test environment adds setup and can differ from production.
Timeouts and worker limits are not hard CPU or total-storage reservations.

decisions.title: Representative test authority
decisions.chosen: Propose scoped monitoring, enrolled representative requests and separate repair authority.
decisions.rationale: Aggregate telemetry cannot reconstruct all parameters and application-role context.
tradeoffs: Enrollment adds setup; an SDK could automate examples but increases integration and privacy work.
Grant mechanics, identity lifecycle and redaction still need a live-project probe.

decisions.title: Durable job coordination
decisions.chosen: Require persisted jobs and action intent; choose the queue and reconciliation protocol next.
decisions.rationale: A restart must not lose work or blindly repeat a database mutation.
decisions.strongestAlternative: A dedicated external queue plus PostgreSQL action records.
tradeoffs: A PostgreSQL-backed queue could reduce services but requires leases and recovery design.
Neither queue choice guarantees exactly-once external effects.

decisions.title: Visual development tooling
decisions.chosen: Propose LangSmith Studio connected to a development LangGraph server.
decisions.rationale: Jared wants to see nodes, tool calls and intermediate state.
decisions.strongestAlternative: Use static graph visualization and custom local logs initially.
tradeoffs: Studio account and tracing/export choices remain open.
The design map is not a running agent or customer dashboard.

decisions.title: Connect Supabase onboarding
decisions.chosen: Use Connect Supabase as the customer onboarding entry point. Database provisioning method remains open.
decisions.rationale: Jared selected provider-based connection for the hosted service; authentication and database authority still need separate design.
decisions.strongestAlternative: Manual connection details as the primary customer onboarding flow.
tradeoffs: OAuth adds integration and token-lifecycle work.
A connection button does not itself establish every database repair permission.
Other providers need separate adapters; V1 remains Supabase only.
